A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey, with matching authors, core taxonomy and section structure. Text, equations, figures, tables and references are readable throughout. Neither PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 surveys existing research. Tables 1–2 catalog cited methods and benchmarks; no original experimental, simulation, user-study or empirical data-analysis results are reported.

after.justification: v5 remains a survey. Its additional methods, benchmarks and findings are attributed to cited research, with no original empirical evaluation.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes an operational algorithm or model. v5 adds descriptions of existing methods, including MATEval, without changing a procedure developed by this work.

E1.justification: Neither version actually trains or evaluates models on datasets. Additions concerning long-context evaluation, SQL equivalence and new benchmarks expand the literature surveyed, rather than experimental coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates baselines against a proposed method. Methods listed in the taxonomy and tables are surveyed research, not experimental comparators.

E3.justification: No experimental protocol is introduced or revised for this work. The added scales, reference annotators and metrics in Table 2 describe existing benchmarks, rather than settings used in new evaluations.

E4.justification: Neither version conducts ablations, robustness tests, error analyses or experimental case studies. Added references concerning critique, bias and evaluation do not introduce such analyses by the survey.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals or significance testing for its own measurements. Discussion of judges' uncertainty and bias remains literature exposition.

E6.justification: Section 5.2.2 newly reports Yasunaga et al.'s success in producing human-aligned LLMs with few annotations. This is an added qualitative finding attributed to cited work, not an original experiment or a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: Section 2 retains Equation 1 and the same definitions of point-wise, pair/list-wise, scoring, ranking and selection judgments. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion are unchanged. The central contributions remain the input/output definitions, attribute–methodology–application taxonomy, benchmark catalog and discussion of challenges.

C2.justification: Section 7 retains its substantive explanations, limitations and proposed directions concerning bias, dynamic judgment, self-judging and human involvement. Legal assessments are added as another example of the existing high-stakes risk, without a new failure condition.

D1.justification: The resource website and public paper-list link remain the same. v5 adds a promise to maintain the list, but no changed availability, access instructions or reproducibility information for an implementation.

R1.justification: Sections 3–6 substantially expand literature coverage across personalized and multi-agent judging, long-context evaluation, SQL equivalence, emerging application domains and critique-assisted reasoning. Added benchmark references include RewardBench, VL-RewardBench and JuStRank. The survey's overall positioning beyond NLG evaluation remains intact.

P1.justification: v5 inserts short literature summaries and makes local wording and terminology edits within the existing subsections. The eight-section narrative remains intact, without extensive rewriting or reorganization. Some new citation placeholders and typographical errors reduce polish.

P2.justification: Figure 2 updates its citation lists, and Figure 4 corrects the Interaction label. Table 2 adds RewardBench and VL-RewardBench and drops the separate 350-item JudgeBench row, although JudgeBench remains discussed. The overall table and schematic designs are retained.

improvement.justification: v5 provides a more informative guide through added explanations of long-context evaluation, SQL equivalence and critique-assisted reasoning, together with an expanded benchmark catalog. The core synthesis remains unchanged. New unresolved citations in Figure 2 and Section 6.2 weaken traceability, but the useful coverage and explanatory additions support a modest net improvement.
